title: When iteration does and does not notice a change

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A for-each loop walks an ArrayList holding [a, b, c, d] and calls list.remove("c") when it reaches "c". Per this page, what happens?

options.text: The loop throws ConcurrentModificationException when it asks for the next element
options.says: The page says that happens when the last element is removed; removing the second-to-last ends the loop before the check runs.

options.text: The loop ends with no exception, and "d" is never visited
options.says: The page says removing the second-to-last element makes hasNext() return false, so the last element is silently skipped.

options.text: The loop ends with no exception, and "d" is still visited
options.says: The page says hasNext() returns false after this removal, so the loop stops before "d".

questions.stem: One thread iterates a ConcurrentHashMap while another thread puts a new key into it. Per this page, what does the iterating thread get?

options.text: Each entry at most once, and no ConcurrentModificationException
options.says: The page says a ConcurrentHashMap iterator may reflect later modifications, returns each element at most once and throws no ConcurrentModificationException.

options.text: Each entry of a snapshot taken at the start, new key excluded
options.says: The page gives the frozen snapshot to CopyOnWriteArrayList; the ConcurrentHashMap iterator may reflect modifications made after its creation.

options.text: Each entry read so far, then a ConcurrentModificationException
options.says: The page says the ConcurrentHashMap iterator guarantees that no ConcurrentModificationException is thrown.

origin.section: 6.5.3.3. Concurrent Collections and Their Iteration Guarantees

concepts: A ConcurrentHashMap iterator is weakly consistent: it never throws ConcurrentModificationException, returns each element at most once, and may or may not reflect changes made after it was created.
Removing the second-to-last element of an ArrayList inside a for-each loop throws nothing and silently skips the last element.
